_comment: Geometry regression scenarios. Adding a test is a JSON entry, not new code.
Model defaults these coordinates assume: Box 100 x 75 x 50, Wall_Thickness 1.85,
Post_Diameter 15, side openings 10 wide x 30 tall whose bottom edge sits
All_Openings_Up=5 above the box floor, so an opening spans z 5 to 35.
Front wall band spans y -37.5 (outer) to -35.65 (inner), so probes at y -37.3
with depth 1.4 sit strictly inside the wall and cannot pick up interior floor.
Probes are 1 mm wide on x so they stay inside the opening's rounded ends;
a wider probe clips the corner arc and reads material as a false negative.
solids counts disconnected bodies. Any unexpected increase means geometry has
detached, which looks normal in a render and fails in a slicer.

scenarios._why3: z=20 is the discriminator: material under the bug, empty when fixed.

scenarios._why2: than a foot's 3.75 mm, so the corner feet are clipped to the box's
scenarios._why3: outline. Unclipped, they stood outside the wall, and the crossing
scenarios._why4: arcs left slivers that made every probe here a CGAL error. A top
scenarios._why5: chamfer builds the shell with offset_sweep() rather than cuboid(),
scenarios._why6: so the clip must follow it. The probe sits outside the box's corner
scenarios._why7: arc, centred (54.65, 33.65), and inside the corner foot's, (59, 38).

scenarios.name: snapclip_box_two_slices
scenarios._why: rabbit_clip cantilever seam joints. Solid count is the guard: a
scenarios._why2: clip oriented the wrong way, or one that bridges the preview gap,
scenarios._why3: both show up here and nowhere else.

scenarios.name: snapclip_lid_two_slices
scenarios._why: At the default 5mm preview spacing an 8mm pin used to reach the
scenarios._why2: next piece and fuse the preview into one body.

scenarios.name: snapclip_single_piece_export
scenarios._why: The case that actually gets printed: one piece, one solid, with
scenarios._why2: its pin attached rather than floating.
scenarios._why3: The bbox pins the clip's ORIENTATION, which solid counts cannot.
scenarios._why4: rabbit_clip builds length on Z, width on X, depth on Y, so it needs
scenarios._why5: orient=RIGHT AND spin=90. With orient alone, width (10) lands on Z
scenarios._why6: instead of depth (3), and z-min drops from 0 to about -3.5
scenarios._why7: while the model still renders and still counts as one solid.
scenarios._why8: z-min is 0 since rc.5 (F-51, floor clips below the bed): the clip
scenarios._why9: was centred on the floor and hung 0.575 mm below it, so a slicer
scenarios._why10: stood the whole piece on its clips. It now starts at the floor's
scenarios._why11: bottom face. rc.4 coupons printed with only the clip tabs on the bed.

scenarios.name: tabclip_single_piece_export
scenarios._why: Same measurement for the Tab style, so a change to shared clip
scenarios._why2: placement cannot silently move one style and not the other.
scenarios._why3: The probe proves the F-51 fix kept the full 3 mm clip and raised it
scenarios._why4: rather than shortening it: the tab spans z 0 to 3 at y 25.65-35.65,
scenarios._why5: and the rc.4 tab stopped at 2.425.

probes.why: top of the tab clip, above the 1.85 mm floor

scenarios.name: snapclip_short_length_blocked
scenarios._why: rabbit_clip aborts with 'Pin is too wide for its length', naming
scenarios._why2: neither parameter. The floor is exactly Clip_Tab_Width/2, measured
scenarios._why3: against BOSL2 2.0.747. Fail with something actionable instead.

Clip_Style must be Tab or Snap

scenarios.name: anchor_lid_face_is_the_exposed_side

scenarios._why2: prints face-down, so the face exposed when the box is closed is
scenarios._why3: the model's z=0 face. v1.2.0 placed the interface at Lid_Height +
scenarios._why4: Lid_Lip_Gap_Height, the MATING face, burying it in the closed box.
scenarios._why5: A 6mm marker attached to lid-face must reach BELOW z=0 (to -3).
scenarios._why6: On the wrong face it would sit up around z=+14 instead.

scenarios._why: The floor anchor sits on the interior floor surface at z=1.85
scenarios._why2: (Wall_Thickness), not on the outer bottom at z=0.

scenarios.name: anchor_box_rim
scenarios._why: The rim anchor sits on top of the wall at Box_Height.

scenarios.name: library_mode_renders_nothing
scenarios._why: Render_On_Include=false must suppress the auto-render so the file
scenarios._why2: can be included as a library. OpenSCAD exits 1 when asked to
scenarios._why3: export an empty scene, so a non-zero exit IS the proof here.

scenarios.name: missing_bosl2_fails_legibly
scenarios._why: Without a guard, a missing BOSL2 gives 'Can't open include file'
scenarios._why2: then a wall of 'Ignoring unknown module' warnings, no geometry,
scenarios._why3: and exit code 0. The zero exit makes it look like it worked.
scenarios._why4: Fixture is the model with its include redirected to a library that
scenarios._why5: does not exist; regenerate with scripts/regen_missing_bosl2_fixture.py.

scenarios.name: library_mode_off_still_renders
scenarios._why: Guards the other direction: the default must still auto-render,
scenarios._why2: or opening the file in OpenSCAD would show nothing.

scenarios.name: e04_edge_treatment_box
scenarios._why: Fillet and chamfer route the outer shell through offset_sweep
scenarios._why2: instead of cuboid. The envelope must not move: both treatments
scenarios._why3: cut inward from edges the full-size footprint still reaches.

scenarios._why: The Gridfinity base is dimensioned by the standard, so a fillet
scenarios._why2: on the box bottom would move a mating surface. Since E-12
scenarios._why3: (Gridfinity to spec) every box rounds up to at least one cell, so
scenarios._why4: the base is always present, and this box is 125.5 x 83.5.
